mcqs.question: Which of the following comparisons correctly describes the role of dietary fibre compared to protein in the human body?

options.A: Fibre primarily provides energy, while protein mainly aids digestion.
options.B: Fibre helps regulate blood sugar levels, whereas protein is stored as fat.
options.C: Fibre aids digestion and prevents constipation, while protein is mainly used for building and repairing tissues.
options.D: Fibre is essential for oxygen transport in the blood, whereas protein acts as a structural component of bones.

mcqs.answer: Fibre aids digestion and prevents constipation, while protein is mainly used for building and repairing tissues.
mcqs.explanation: Dietary fibre is indigestible carbohydrate that adds bulk to stool and promotes regular bowel movements. Protein, on the other hand, supplies amino acids needed for growth, tissue repair, and enzyme production. Options A, B, and D describe inaccurate functions for fibre or protein.

mcqs.learning_point: Effect of excessive consumption of particular foods
mcqs.question: In a competitive exam, which pair of health problems is most directly linked to excessive consumption of salty snacks?

options.A: Weight gain and vitamin D deficiency
options.B: High blood pressure and kidney strain
options.C: Dental caries and iron deficiency anemia

mcqs.answer: High blood pressure and kidney strain
mcqs.explanation: Salty snacks contain high sodium, which raises blood pressure and forces the kidneys to work harder to excrete excess salt, potentially leading to kidney strain. The other options pair conditions that are not primarily caused by high salt intake.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a simple way for a student to make a healthier food choice at school?

options.A: Choosing a chocolate bar instead of an apple
options.B: Drinking a soda with a meal
options.C: Selecting a fruit cup instead of fried chips
options.D: Skipping lunch to avoid extra calories

mcqs.answer: Selecting a fruit cup instead of fried chips
mcqs.explanation: Replacing fried, high‑fat snacks with a fruit cup adds vitamins, fibre, and natural sugars, making the meal healthier. Options A and B add more sugar and unhealthy fats, while D can lead to nutrient deficiency.

mcqs.question: What does a balanced diet mean for a growing child?

options.A: Eating only fruits and vegetables every day
options.B: Consuming all food groups in the right proportions to meet nutritional needs
options.C: Avoiding all fats and sugars completely
options.D: Eating the same amount of food at every meal

mcqs.answer: Consuming all food groups in the right proportions to meet nutritional needs
mcqs.explanation: A balanced diet provides carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, and water in appropriate amounts. Options A, C, and D are too restrictive or ignore the need for variety and proportion.

mcqs.learning_point: Need for different nutrients in suitable amounts
mcqs.question: Which statement best defines why the body needs different nutrients in suitable amounts?

options.A: All nutrients perform the same function, so the body only needs a large amount of any one of them.
options.B: Each nutrient has a specific role, and the body requires them in particular proportions for optimal health.
options.C: Only vitamins are essential; minerals and proteins are optional.
options.D: The body can store unlimited amounts of every nutrient without any adverse effects.

mcqs.answer: Each nutrient has a specific role, and the body requires them in particular proportions for optimal health.
mcqs.explanation: Proteins build tissues, carbohydrates supply energy, fats support cell membranes, vitamins and minerals act as co‑factors, and water maintains fluid balance. The correct balance prevents deficiencies and excesses. Options A, C, and D are scientifically inaccurate.

mcqs.question: Riya eats the same three dishes every day. Which action would best improve the variety in her diet?

options.A: Add a different coloured fruit or vegetable to her plate each day
options.B: Increase the portion size of the same dishes
options.C: Replace water with a sugary drink
options.D: Eat the same meals but at a later time

mcqs.answer: Add a different coloured fruit or vegetable to her plate each day
mcqs.explanation: Different colours usually indicate different nutrients and phytochemicals, enhancing dietary variety. Options B, C, and D do not introduce new nutrients and may even be detrimental.

mcqs.question: Which of the following examples best illustrates why drinking enough water is important for the body?

options.A: Water helps the skin stay dry during hot weather.
options.B: Water enables the body to regulate temperature by sweating.
options.C: Water replaces the need for vitamins in the diet.

mcqs.answer: Water enables the body to regulate temperature by sweating.
mcqs.explanation: When the body gets hot, water loss through sweat cools the skin, maintaining a stable internal temperature. Options A, C, and D misrepresent water’s primary physiological roles.

mcqs.question: Sam often feels constipated because he eats very little fruit, vegetables, or whole grains. Which change would most effectively increase his fibre intake?

options.A: Replace his daily soda with a glass of milk.
options.B: Add a bowl of mixed beans to his lunch three times a week.
options.C: Eat an extra piece of cheese after dinner.
options.D: Increase his portion of fried chicken.

mcqs.answer: Add a bowl of mixed beans to his lunch three times a week.
mcqs.explanation: Beans are rich in dietary fibre, which helps soften stool and promote regular bowel movements. Options A, C, and D do not provide significant fibre and may not address the problem.
